resources.string: Start with your first connection, or choose the task you need.
Join the network, check the picture, then drive.
For a direct connection, join the robot’s Wi-Fi. In router mode, connect the robot and this device to the same network. Use the connection guide, then search for the robot.
Check that cables, parts and battery are secure. Choose level ground with room to move. After connecting, check the robot and battery on home. Review any reported problems in robot maintenance.
Select Cockpit on robot home and wait for a live picture. Start with a short movement at a low gear. Release the controls and check that the robot stops, then leave the cockpit when finished.
Directions, gears, firing and interrupted control.
The left stick moves the chassis; the right stick aims the gimbal. Use WASD to move, Q/E to turn and arrow keys to aim. See Settings → Shortcuts for current bindings. Start at a low gear.

Switch infrared or gel beads in the firing area. Holding fire repeats shots. Before gel-bead use, check the selected mode, target and surroundings. Never fire at people or animals or aim the trajectory light at eyes. Release fire before other tasks.

Release sticks or keys to request a stop. Esc leaves the cockpit; with mouse aiming active it releases the mouse first. Stale video, focus loss or disconnection stops control. After recovery, check the robot is still before entering or using fresh input.
Select, confirm, then stop or take control.

Return to 1× view in the cockpit and open Object following. Use steady lighting and a target distinct from the background. Keep it visible and leave room to move. Occlusion, sudden turns or lighting changes can affect detection.

Select a target box, wait for a lock and check the selection. Following starts only after Start following is confirmed. A lock is not a running follow. Manual motion and firing are restricted while following.

Use Stop following or directional input to take control. Target loss or a video/link interruption also cancels following. If stopping is unconfirmed, check the robot and retry the stop. Recovery requires a new selection and confirmation.
Place markers and complete manual challenges.
Open Challenge in the cockpit. Practice uses numbered markers 1–5 and timed targets. Race lets you choose a target count and finish them in any order. Keep markers clearly visible.

Practice uses infrared. Race supports infrared or gel beads; use knock-down targets for gel-bead races. Host scoring uses detections and firing reports. A hit cue is not armor confirmation or proof of a physical shot. Mute cues in setup if needed.

Controls are locked during preparation and results. Drive manually during play. Review time, checkpoints or score, save a name to this session’s results and try again. Retry stopping if cleanup is unconfirmed. Challenges do not drive automatically.
Distinguish robot SD media from local captures.

Local capture and robot SD capture are separate cockpit tasks. Local capture saves the received picture; SD capture is performed by the robot camera. Explicitly stop an active recording before leaving the capture task.

Refresh the robot album and choose a photo or recording to download. Play or export after the download finishes. A failed download or disconnection leaves the original file on the robot; reconnect and retry.

Check SD status and space in Settings → Media. Formatting deletes files on the card. Download and export anything needed before confirming it. Resolve an active capture or unknown result before clearing space.
Start from a local example and observe its lifecycle.
Open a local preset or create a Python script in the library. Read it first and identify any movement, firing or accessory actions. Save edits, then check the connected robot before running.

Run prepares and uploads the program, then waits for onboard state. Upload completion is not proof that execution started. Observe status, logs and the program panel. Stop the current program before another control task.

Select Stop and wait for confirmation. If the link or stop result is unknown, leaving the page does not prove the onboard program ended. Reconnect to the same robot, check its state, then prepare the next run.
Wiring, module identity, binding and calibration.
Install the arm by module identity

Power off before wiring. Address modules if needed, then use Identify in arm management to check and bind the main and secondary servos. Follow device calibration poses. After verifying configuration, use the cockpit for a low-speed check.
Health, addressing, calibration and local firmware.

End driving, recording and scripts, then power off before checking loose cables, screws, wheels or installed parts. Repeated configuration writes do not resolve a mechanical obstruction. Address the physical issue before powering on to inspect reports.

Review battery, module health, product and versions in robot maintenance. Check report freshness: disconnected or stale data is not current state. Choose inspection, addressing or calibration for the reported issue; run one maintenance task at a time.

Use module addressing to identify and number parts. Lift all four wheels for motor procedures and follow the displayed physical positions. Connect one unnumbered accessory at a time. End testing and verify before leaving; assigned IDs are not undone by exit.

Select the required calibration, keep the robot still and leave space for gimbal movement. Follow each displayed pose and wait for a terminal report. Canceling, leaving or reconnecting does not prove success or undo written results.
Verify local firmware and its result

Read device configuration, then select and validate matching local firmware. Keep the battery above 50%% and check the target and modules. After transfer, wait for installation and reboot, then verify versions. Stopping local transfer does not cancel onboard flashing.
